questionText: Arjun is 47 years old and Riya is 9 years old. What was the difference in their ages 6 years ago?
hints: This is about the gap between two people's ages. Think about what happens to that gap as both of them grow older together.
Find how old Arjun and Riya each were 6 years ago. Then compare those two ages with each other.
Similar example: Meena is 25 and Tara is 9. Four years ago Meena was 21 and Tara was 5. 21 − 5 = 16, and today 25 − 9 = 16 as well. The gap stays the same.

stepByStep.text: Find Arjun's age 6 years ago.
Find Riya's age 6 years ago.
Subtract to find the difference in their ages at that time.
This is the same as the difference today, because both of them grew older by the same 6 years. So the difference was 38.

misconceptions.A: It looks as if 6 was taken away from the gap. Both of them were 6 years younger then, so the gap between them did not change.
misconceptions.B: This is Arjun's age 6 years ago, not the gap. Riya was 6 years younger then too, so subtract one age from the other.
misconceptions.C: It looks as if 6 was added to the gap. Both of them were 6 years younger then, so the gap between them did not change.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Back then Arjun was 41 and Riya was 3, and 41 − 3 = 38. The gap between two ages never changes.

questionText: Arjun is 27 years old and Riya is 28 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 10 years?
hints: This is an age problem. Everybody grows older by the same number of years, so think about each person's age in the future before you add.
Find how old Arjun will be after 10 years. Then do the same for Riya.

Here is a similar one. Meena is 12 years old and Kabir is 15 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 5 years? Meena will be 12 + 5 = 17 and Kabir will be 15 + 5 = 20, so the sum will be 17 + 20 = 37.

stepByStep.text: After 10 years Arjun will be 27 + 10 = 37 years old.
Riya will be 28 + 10 = 38 years old.
Now add the two new ages: 37 + 38 = 75. So the sum of their ages after 10 years will be 75.

misconceptions.A: 65 is 27 + 28 + 10, so only one of them got older. Arjun and Riya each gain 10 years.
misconceptions.B: Yes! In 10 years each of them is 10 older, so 37 + 38 = 75.
misconceptions.C: 55 is 27 + 28, the sum of their ages now. First make each of them 10 years older.
misconceptions.D: 85 is a little too big: the 10 years were counted once more than needed. Each of the two people gets older just once.

questionText: Siya is 40 years old and Aditya is 34 years old. What was the difference in their ages 10 years ago?
hints: This question is about the gap between two ages. Think about what happens to that gap when both people are younger by the same number of years.
Find how old Siya and Aditya each were 10 years ago. Then see how far apart those two ages are.

Here is a similar one. Asha is 25 years old and Ravi is 16 years old. What was the difference in their ages 4 years ago? 4 years ago Asha was 25 − 4 = 21 and Ravi was 16 − 4 = 12. The difference was 21 − 12 = 9.

stepByStep.text: 10 years ago Siya was 40 − 10 = 30 years old and Aditya was 34 − 10 = 24 years old.
The difference then was 30 − 24 = 6.
That is the same as today, 40 − 34 = 6, because both of them were 10 years younger. The difference in their ages was 6.

misconceptions.A: 16 comes from 40 − 34 + 10. Both of them were 10 years younger, so does the gap between them change at all?
misconceptions.B: 30 is how old Siya was 10 years ago, 40 − 10. The question asks how far apart the two ages were.
misconceptions.C: 24 is Aditya's age 10 years ago, 34 − 10. That is one person's age, but the question is about the gap between the two.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Both were 10 years younger then, so the gap between them stays the same: 40 − 34 = 6.

questionText: Riya is 26 years old and Rohan is 11 years old. What was the difference in their ages 3 years ago?
hints: This is about the gap between two people's ages. Think about what happens to that gap as both of them grow older together.
Find how old Riya and Rohan each were 3 years ago. Then compare those two ages with each other.
Similar example: Dev is 40 and Isha is 18. Five years ago Dev was 35 and Isha was 13. 35 − 13 = 22, and today 40 − 18 = 22 as well. The gap stays the same.

stepByStep.text: Find Riya's age 3 years ago.
Find Rohan's age 3 years ago.
Subtract to find the difference in their ages at that time.
This is the same as the difference today, because both of them grew older by the same 3 years. So the difference was 15.

misconceptions.A: This is Riya's age 3 years ago, not the gap. Rohan was 3 years younger then too, so subtract one age from the other.
misconceptions.B: It looks as if 3 was added to the gap. Both of them were 3 years younger then, so the gap between them did not change.
misconceptions.C: It looks as if 3 was taken away from the gap. Both of them were 3 years younger then, so the gap between them did not change.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Back then Riya was 23 and Rohan was 8, and 23 − 8 = 15. The gap between two ages never changes.

questionText: Tara is 35 years old and Dev is 31 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 4 years?
hints: This is an age problem. Everybody grows older by the same number of years, so think about each person's age in the future before you add.
Find how old Tara will be after 4 years. Then do the same for Dev.

Here is a similar one. Asha is 12 years old and Ravi is 15 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 5 years? Asha will be 12 + 5 = 17 and Ravi will be 15 + 5 = 20, so the sum will be 17 + 20 = 37.

stepByStep.text: After 4 years Tara will be 35 + 4 = 39 years old.
Dev will be 31 + 4 = 35 years old.
Add the two new ages: 39 + 35 = 74. The sum of their ages will be 74.

misconceptions.A: Yes! Tara will be 39 and Dev will be 35, and 39 + 35 = 74.
misconceptions.B: 70 adds the 4 years only once, 35 + 31 + 4. Both Tara and Dev grow 4 years older.
misconceptions.C: 66 is 35 + 31, the sum of their ages now. First make each of them 4 years older.
misconceptions.D: 78 has the 4 years in it one time too many. Make Tara and Dev 4 years older, add their two new ages, and then stop.

questionText: Mother+daughter ages 5yr ago sum=5x. Sum 5yr hence?
hints: This is an age problem with two people. When time passes, each person gets older, so the sum of their ages grows for both of them.
From 5 years ago to 5 years from now is 10 years. Think about how much each of the two people adds to the sum in that time.

Similar example: 3 years ago, the ages of a father and son added up to 40. From 3 years ago to 3 years from now is 6 years. Two people each grow 6 years older, so the sum grows by 2 × 6 = 12. The sum 3 years from now is 40 + 12 = 52.

stepByStep.text: From 5 years ago to 5 years from now is 10 years.
There are two people, the mother and the daughter. Each one grows 10 years older, so the sum grows by 20.
The sum 5 years ago was 5x. So the sum of their ages 5 years from now is 5x + 20.

misconceptions.A: This takes 10 away. Ages grow as time passes, so the sum must go up, and it goes up for both people.
misconceptions.B: The 20 is right, but it should be added. Going forward in time makes both people older.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 10 years pass for two people, so the sum grows by 2 × 10 = 20.
misconceptions.D: This adds 10 years for only one person. Both the mother and the daughter grow 10 years older.

questionText: Husband+wife age 6yr ago=48. Present H+W+Son=63. Son's age 6yr hence?
hints: This is an age problem. First bring everyone to the same time, the present, before you compare the sums.
Find the sum of the husband's and wife's ages now. Two people each grew 6 years older since then.

Similar example: 4 years ago a father's and mother's ages added up to 50. Now their sum is 50 + 2 × 4 = 58. Father, mother and daughter add up to 66 now, so the daughter is 66 − 58 = 8 now. In 4 years she will be 8 + 4 = 12.

stepByStep.text: 6 years ago the husband and wife together were 48. Each is 6 years older now, so add 12.
Now all three together are 63. Take away the husband and wife to get the son's age now.
Add 6 years to find the son's age 6 years from now.
The son will be 9 years old.

misconceptions.A: Check the sum of the husband's and wife's ages now. Two people each grew 6 years older, so add 12 to 48. Then find the son's age.
misconceptions.B: 6 is the number of years that pass, not the son's age. Find his age now, then add 6.
misconceptions.C: Go through it step by step: the couple's sum now, then the son's age now, then 6 years on.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The couple are 60 together now, so the son is 3, and in 6 years he will be 9.

questionText: Sum of ages of Nirav and Vipul 3 yrs ago was 38. Vipul's age after 2 yrs if he is 2 yrs younger than Nirav?
hints: This is an age problem about two people. Bring the sum to the present first, then split it using the difference in their ages.
Find the sum of their ages now. Each of the two boys is 3 years older than he was 3 years ago.

Similar example: 2 years ago the ages of Asha and Ravi added up to 26. Now the sum is 26 + 2 × 2 = 30. Ravi is 4 years younger, so take 4 away and halve: (30 − 4) ÷ 2 = 13. Ravi is 13 now. After 3 years he will be 13 + 3 = 16.

stepByStep.text: 3 years ago the sum was 38. Both are 3 years older now, so add 6.
Vipul is 2 years younger. Take away Nirav's 2 extra years, then share equally.
Vipul is 21 now. Add 2 years.
After 2 years Vipul will be 23 years old.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The sum now is 44, Vipul is 21 now, and after 2 years he is 23 years old.
misconceptions.B: 22 is half of the sum now. The two are not the same age, and the question asks for Vipul's age after 2 years.
misconceptions.C: This is Nirav's age after 2 years. Vipul is the younger one.
misconceptions.D: This shares the sum equally and adds 2. Vipul is 2 years younger than Nirav, so allow for that before you halve.

questionText: Asha is 9 years old now. How old will she be after 6 years?
hints: As the years pass, a person's age goes up by the same number of years.
Add the 6 years to Asha's age now.
Example: Raju is 7 now. After 5 years he will be 7 + 5 = 12 years old.

stepByStep.text: Asha is 9 now.
After 6 years her age goes up by 6: 9 + 6 = 15.
So Asha will be 15 years old.

misconceptions.A: 3 is 9 − 6, her age 6 years ago. The word after means going forward in time, so add.
misconceptions.B: 54 is 9 × 6. Each year adds just 1 to her age, so add 6.
misconceptions.D: 14 is one short. Count on 6 from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15.

questionText: Meera is 10 years old and her father is 38 years old. How many years older than Meera is her father?
hints: The words how many years older ask for the gap between the two ages.
Subtract Meera's age from her father's age.
Example: a boy is 8 and his mother is 33. She is 33 − 8 = 25 years older.

stepByStep.text: Her father is 38 and Meera is 10.
So her father is 28 years older.

misconceptions.A: 48 is 38 + 10. To find how much older, subtract.
misconceptions.B: 18 takes away one ten too many. 38 − 10 = 28.
misconceptions.C: 38 is the father's age. The question asks how much older he is than Meera.

questionText: Tina is 8 years old. Her mother is 4 times as old as Tina. How old is her mother?
hints: The words times as old tell you to multiply.
Multiply Tina's age by 4.
Example: Sunil is 6 and his father is 5 times as old, so his father is 6 × 5 = 30.

stepByStep.text: Tina is 8.
Her mother is 4 times as old: 8 × 4 = 32.
So her mother is 32 years old.

misconceptions.B: 12 is 8 + 4. The words 4 times as old mean multiply by 4.
misconceptions.C: 2 is 8 ÷ 4. Her mother is older than Tina, so multiply.

questionText: Four years ago, Zoya was 6 years old. How old is she now?
hints: The words years ago take you into the past. Coming back to today, the age goes up.
She was 6 then, and 4 years have passed since. Add.
Example: three years ago Kabir was 9, so now he is 9 + 3 = 12.

stepByStep.text: Four years ago Zoya was 6.
Since then 4 years have passed: 6 + 4 = 10.
So Zoya is 10 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 2 is 6 − 4. She was 6 in the past, so today she is older, not younger.
misconceptions.C: 24 is 6 × 4. Each year adds 1 to her age, so add 4.
misconceptions.D: 6 was her age four years ago. Add the 4 years that have passed.

questionText: Dev was born in the year 2015. How old was he on his birthday in 2024?
hints: Age on a birthday is the number of years from the birth year to that year.
Subtract the birth year from 2024.
Example: someone born in 2010 turns 2021 − 2010 = 11 on the birthday in 2021.

stepByStep.text: Dev was born in 2015.
So Dev was 9 years old on his birthday in 2024.

misconceptions.A: 10 counts both 2015 and 2024. In 2015 he was just born, so count the steps between the years: 9.
misconceptions.B: 8 is one short. From 2015 to 2024 is 9 years.
misconceptions.D: 19 has an extra ten. 2015 to 2025 would be 10 years, so 2015 to 2024 is 9.

questionText: Rohan's father is 36 years old. Rohan is one-third as old as his father. How old is Rohan?
hints: One-third as old means the age is split into 3 equal parts and you take one of them.
Divide the father's age by 3.
Example: a mother is 40 and her son is one-quarter as old, so the son is 40 ÷ 4 = 10.

stepByStep.text: His father is 36.
One-third of 36 is 36 ÷ 3 = 12.
So Rohan is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 33 is 36 − 3. One-third means divide by 3.
misconceptions.B: 108 is 36 × 3. Rohan is younger than his father, so divide.
misconceptions.C: 18 is half of 36. One-third means 3 equal parts: 36 ÷ 3.

questionText: Anil is 3 years older than his brother Sunil today. How many years older than Sunil will Anil be after 10 years?
hints: Think about what happens to both brothers as the years go by. Do they grow older at the same pace?
Try it with ages you choose: say Sunil is 5 and Anil is 8. Find both ages after 10 years.
Example: Rita is 4 years older than Gita. If Gita is 6 and Rita is 10, then after 5 years they are 11 and 15, and Rita is still 15 − 11 = 4 years older.

stepByStep.text: Suppose Sunil is 5, so Anil is 8.
After 10 years Sunil is 15 and Anil is 18.
18 − 15 = 3. Both grow older by the same amount, so the gap stays the same.
So Anil will still be 3 years older.

misconceptions.A: Right! Both brothers grow 10 years older, so the gap stays 3.
misconceptions.B: 13 is 3 + 10. Sunil also grows 10 years older, so the gap does not grow.
misconceptions.C: 7 is 10 − 3. The gap between two people's ages never changes.
misconceptions.D: 30 is 3 × 10. The gap stays the same every year.

questionText: Ravi is 12 years old now. In how many years will he be 20 years old?
hints: You know the age now and the age later. The number of years in between is the gap.
Subtract Ravi's age now from 20.
Example: Simran is 9 now. She will be 15 in 15 − 9 = 6 years.

stepByStep.text: Ravi is 12 now and will be 20 later.
So Ravi will be 20 in 8 years.

misconceptions.A: 32 is 20 + 12. The question asks for the years in between, so subtract.
misconceptions.C: 7 is one short: 12 + 7 = 19. One more year is needed.
misconceptions.D: 9 is one too many: 12 + 9 = 21. Count on from 12 to 20.

questionText: Amit is 3 years older than Bina. Bina is 2 years older than Chirag. Chirag is 7 years old. How old is Amit?
hints: Start from the person whose age you know and work along the chain, one person at a time.
Chirag is 7 and Bina is 2 years older. Find Bina's age first.
Example: Pari is 4 years older than Qasim, Qasim is 1 year older than Ria, and Ria is 6. Then Qasim is 7 and Pari is 7 + 4 = 11.

stepByStep.text: Bina is 2 years older than Chirag: 7 + 2 = 9.
Amit is 3 years older than Bina: 9 + 3 = 12.
So Amit is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 9 is Bina's age. Amit is 3 years older than Bina.
misconceptions.B: 10 is 7 + 3, which skips Bina. Amit is 3 years older than Bina, and Bina is 9.
misconceptions.C: Right! Chirag is 7, Bina is 9 and Amit is 12.
misconceptions.D: 2 comes from subtracting both gaps. Amit is the oldest of the three, so add.

questionText: Farhan is 11 years old. His sister Rehana is 3 years younger than him. How old was Rehana 2 years ago?
hints: Find the sister's age now first. Then go back in time.
Rehana is 3 years younger than Farhan: 11 − 3.
Example: Mohan is 16 and his sister is 2 years younger, so she is 14. Five years ago she was 14 − 5 = 9.

stepByStep.text: Rehana's age now: 11 − 3 = 8.
Two years ago she was 2 years younger: 8 − 2 = 6.
So Rehana was 6 years old.

misconceptions.A: 8 is Rehana's age now. The question asks about 2 years ago.
misconceptions.B: 12 comes from adding the 3 years. Rehana is younger than Farhan, so subtract.
misconceptions.C: 10 is 8 + 2, her age two years from now. The word ago means going back.
misconceptions.D: Yes! She is 8 now, so two years ago she was 6.

questionText: Diya is 7 years old and her mother is 35 years old. After 7 years, how many times as old as Diya will her mother be?
hints: Both people grow older. Find both new ages first, then compare them by dividing.
After 7 years, Diya will be 7 + 7 and her mother will be 35 + 7.
Example: a boy is 4 and his father is 34. After 2 years they are 6 and 36, and 36 ÷ 6 = 6, so the father is 6 times as old.

stepByStep.text: After 7 years Diya will be 7 + 7 = 14.
Her mother will be 35 + 7 = 42.
So her mother will be 3 times as old as Diya.

misconceptions.A: Right! 42 is 3 times 14.
misconceptions.B: 5 times is true today, since 35 ÷ 7 = 5. After 7 years both ages change.
misconceptions.C: Check the dividing: 14 × 4 = 56, which is more than 42. Try 14 × 3.
misconceptions.D: 28 is the gap between their ages, which never changes. The words how many times ask you to divide.

questionText: The sum of the ages of Anu and her mother is 44 years. Anu is 8 years old. How old was her mother when Anu was born?
hints: Find the mother's age now. Then go back to the year Anu was born.
Mother's age now: 44 − 8.
Example: a boy of 5 and his father have ages adding up to 40. The father is 35 now, and when the boy was born, 5 years ago, he was 35 − 5 = 30.

stepByStep.text: Mother's age now: 44 − 8 = 36.
Anu was born 8 years ago.
Her mother was then 36 − 8 = 28.
So her mother was 28 years old when Anu was born.

misconceptions.A: 36 is her mother's age now. Anu was born 8 years ago, so go back 8 years.
misconceptions.B: Yes! She is 36 now, so she was 28 when Anu was born.
misconceptions.C: 44 is the two ages together. Take away Anu's 8 to get her mother's age, then go back 8 years.
misconceptions.D: 52 is 44 + 8. Take Anu's age away from the sum instead.

questionText: The ages of two sisters add up to 20 years. One sister is 4 years older than the other. How old is the older sister?
hints: You know the sum and the difference of two ages. Take away the extra years and the rest splits equally.
Take the extra 4 years away from 20. What is left is twice the younger sister's age.
Example: two ages add up to 34 and differ by 6. 34 − 6 = 28, and half of 28 is 14, so the younger is 14 and the older is 14 + 6 = 20.

stepByStep.text: Take away the extra years: 20 − 4 = 16.
Half of 16 is 8, so the younger sister is 8.
The older sister is 8 + 4 = 12.
So the older sister is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 8 is the younger sister's age. Add 4 for the older sister.
misconceptions.B: 16 is 20 − 4. It still has to be split between the two sisters.
misconceptions.C: Right! The sisters are 8 and 12: together 20, and 4 apart.
misconceptions.D: 10 is half of 20, which would make the sisters the same age. One is 4 years older.

questionText: A father is 3 times as old as his son. Their ages add up to 48 years. How old is the son?
hints: Think of the son's age as 1 part. Then the father's age is a number of the same parts, and you can count all the parts in the sum.
The son is 1 part and the father is 3 parts. That makes 4 parts adding up to 48.
Example: a mother is 4 times as old as her daughter and their ages add up to 40. That is 5 parts, so the daughter is 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

stepByStep.text: The son is 1 part and the father is 3 parts, so together they are 4 parts.
4 parts are 48, so one part is 48 ÷ 4 = 12.
So the son is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 16 is 48 ÷ 3. Count the son's own part too: there are 4 parts in all.
misconceptions.B: 36 is the father's age. The son is one part: 12.
misconceptions.C: 24 is half of 48, which would make them the same age. The father has 3 parts and the son has 1.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The son is 12 and the father is 36: together 48.

questionText: Three years ago, Kiran was 9 years old. How old will she be 4 years from now?
hints: Move along the timeline in two jumps: from the past to today, then from today to the future.
First find Kiran's age today: 9 + 3.
Example: four years ago Jai was 5, so he is 9 now. Two years from now he will be 9 + 2 = 11.

stepByStep.text: Kiran's age today: 9 + 3 = 12.
Four years from now: 12 + 4 = 16.
So Kiran will be 16 years old.

misconceptions.A: Right! She was 9 then, is 12 now, and will be 16 four years from now.
misconceptions.B: 13 is 9 + 4, which skips the 3 years that have already passed. Find her age today first.
misconceptions.C: 10 takes away 3 instead of adding. She was 9 in the past, so today she is 12.
misconceptions.D: 12 is Kiran's age today. Go 4 more years ahead.

questionText: The ages of Geeta and Hari add up to 25 years now. What did their ages add up to 3 years ago?
hints: Going back in time changes the age of each person, not just one. Count how many people are in the sum.
Three years ago Geeta was 3 years younger, and so was Hari. How much smaller was the sum?
Example: two friends' ages add up to 30. Five years ago each was 5 years younger, so the sum was 30 − 5 − 5 = 20.

stepByStep.text: Three years ago Geeta was 3 years younger and Hari was 3 years younger.
Together that is 3 + 3 = 6 years less.
25 − 6 = 19, so their ages added up to 19 years.

misconceptions.A: 22 takes away 3 only once. Both Geeta and Hari were 3 years younger.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Each was 3 years younger, so the sum was 6 less: 19.
misconceptions.C: 28 adds 3. The word ago goes back in time, so the ages were smaller.
misconceptions.D: 31 adds 6. The word ago goes back in time, so take 6 away instead.

questionText: Jay's grandfather is 72 years old. Jay's father is half as old as the grandfather. Jay is one-quarter as old as his father. How old is Jay?
hints: Work down the family one step at a time, using each age to find the next.
Find the father's age first: half of 72.
Example: a grandmother is 60, the mother is half as old, so 30, and the child is one-fifth as old as the mother: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

stepByStep.text: Father's age: 72 ÷ 2 = 36.
Jay's age is one-quarter of 36: 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
So Jay is 9 years old.

misconceptions.A: 18 is one-quarter of the grandfather's age. Jay's age is one-quarter of his father's age, 36.
misconceptions.B: 36 is the father's age. Now take one-quarter of it.
misconceptions.C: Right! The father is 36, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
misconceptions.D: 12 is 36 ÷ 3. One-quarter means 4 equal parts: 36 ÷ 4.

questionText: Varun is 9 years old. His father is 27 years older than him. How old will his father be when Varun is 15?
hints: The gap between two people's ages stays the same for ever. Use it at the later time.
When Varun is 15, his father will still be 27 years older than him.
Example: Nita is 6 and her mother is 24 years older. When Nita is 10, her mother will be 10 + 24 = 34.

stepByStep.text: The father is always 27 years older than Varun.
When Varun is 15, his father will be 15 + 27 = 42.
So his father will be 42 years old.

misconceptions.A: 36 is the father's age now, 9 + 27. By the time Varun is 15, six more years have passed.
misconceptions.B: 33 is 27 + 6. The 27 is the gap, not the father's age: his age now is 36.
misconceptions.C: 51 is 36 + 15. Only 6 years pass between Varun being 9 and 15, so add 6 to 36.

questionText: Rahul is 10 years old and his father is 40 years old. After how many years will the father be 3 times as old as Rahul?
hints: Both ages go up together. Try a number of years, find both new ages, and check whether one is 3 times the other.
Try each choice. After 10 years they would be 20 and 50. Is 50 equal to 3 times 20?
Example: a girl is 6 and her mother is 30. After 2 years they are 8 and 32, and 32 is 4 times 8, so after 2 years the mother is 4 times as old.

stepByStep.text: After 5 years Rahul will be 10 + 5 = 15.
His father will be 40 + 5 = 45.
45 is 3 times 15, so the father is then 3 times as old.
So it happens after 5 years.

misconceptions.A: Right! After 5 years they are 15 and 45, and 45 is 3 times 15.
misconceptions.B: After 10 years they are 20 and 50, but 3 times 20 is 60. Try fewer years.
misconceptions.C: After 15 years they are 25 and 55, but 3 times 25 is 75. Try fewer years.
misconceptions.D: After 20 years they are 30 and 60, and 60 is only 2 times 30. Try fewer years.

questionText: Ali is 14 years old and his sister Sara is 8 years old. How old was Ali when Sara was exactly half his age?
hints: The gap between their ages never changes. When one person is half the other's age, the younger one's age equals the gap.
Find the gap: 14 − 8. When Sara's age was equal to this gap, Ali was twice as old as her.
Example: Ravi is 15 and Mala is 11, a gap of 4. When Mala was 4, Ravi was 4 + 4 = 8, exactly double.

stepByStep.text: Ali is always 14 − 8 = 6 years older than Sara.
Sara is half Ali's age when her age equals the gap, so Sara was 6.
Ali was then 6 + 6 = 12.
So Ali was 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 7 is half of Ali's age today. When Ali was 7, Sara was only 1. Use the gap of 6 years.
misconceptions.B: Yes! When Ali was 12, Sara was 6, exactly half.
misconceptions.C: 6 was Sara's age at that time. The question asks for Ali's age.
misconceptions.D: When Ali was 10, Sara was 4, and half of 10 is 5. Go to the time when Sara was 6.

questionText: Five years ago, a mother was 7 times as old as her daughter. The mother is 33 years old now. How old is the daughter now?
hints: Go back to the time the clue talks about, work out the ages then, and return to today.
Find the mother's age five years ago: 33 − 5.
Example: four years ago a father was 6 times as old as his son. The father is 40 now, so he was 36 then and the son was 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Today the son is 6 + 4 = 10.

stepByStep.text: Five years ago the mother was 33 − 5 = 28.
The daughter was then 28 ÷ 7 = 4.
Today the daughter is 4 + 5 = 9.
So the daughter is 9 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 4 was the daughter's age five years ago. Add the 5 years to come back to today.
misconceptions.B: 14 adds the 5 years twice. From 4, add 5 just once.
misconceptions.C: Right! She was 4 then, so she is 9 now.
misconceptions.D: 28 was the mother's age five years ago. Divide by 7 for the daughter's age then, and come back to today.

questionText: Aman is twice as old as Bhavna. Four years ago, Aman was three times as old as Bhavna was then. How old is Bhavna now?
hints: Two clues must both be true. Try an age, use the first clue to get the other age, then test the second clue.
Try a choice: if Bhavna is 12, Aman is 24. Four years ago they were 8 and 20. Is 20 three times 8?
Example: Meena is twice as old as Nitu, and five years ago she was three times as old. Try Nitu 10 and Meena 20: five years ago they were 5 and 15, and 15 is 3 times 5. So Nitu is 10.

stepByStep.text: Try Bhavna as 8: then Aman is 2 × 8 = 16.
Four years ago Bhavna was 8 − 4 = 4 and Aman was 16 − 4 = 12.
12 is 3 times 4, so both clues fit.
So Bhavna is 8 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 16 is Aman's age. The question asks for Bhavna, who is half as old.
misconceptions.B: 4 was Bhavna's age four years ago. Add the 4 years to come back to today.
misconceptions.C: If Bhavna were 12, Aman would be 24, and four years ago they would be 8 and 20. But 3 times 8 is 24, not 20.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Bhavna is 8 and Aman is 16 now; four years ago they were 4 and 12, and 12 is 3 times 4.

questionText: A grandfather is 9 times as old as his grandson. Their ages add up to 70 years. How old will the grandfather be when the grandson is 10 years old?
hints: Use parts to find both ages now. Then move both people forward by the same number of years.
The grandson is 1 part and the grandfather is 9 parts, so 10 parts make 70. Find one part.
Example: a father is 5 times as old as his daughter and their ages add up to 36. Six parts make 36, so she is 6 and he is 30. When she is 8, two years later, he will be 30 + 2 = 32.

stepByStep.text: The grandson is 1 part and the grandfather is 9 parts. 10 parts are 70, so one part is 70 ÷ 10 = 7.
The grandson is 7 and the grandfather is 9 × 7 = 63.
The grandson will be 10 after 10 − 7 = 3 years.
63 + 3 = 66, so the grandfather will be 66 years old.

misconceptions.A: Right! He is 63 now, and 3 years later he is 66.
misconceptions.B: 63 is the grandfather's age now. The grandson is 7 now, so move 3 years ahead.
misconceptions.C: 73 adds 10 years. The grandson needs only 3 more years to reach 10.
misconceptions.D: 90 is 9 × 10. He is 9 times as old only now; later, both simply grow older by the same number of years.

questionText: Neel says that in 6 years he will be twice as old as he was 2 years ago. How old is Neel now?
hints: Compare two moments: one in the past and one in the future. Count the years between them.
From 2 years ago to 6 years from now is 2 + 6 = 8 years. In those 8 years his age doubles.
Example: in 5 years Tanu will be twice as old as she was 1 year ago. Those moments are 6 years apart, so she was 6 one year ago, and she is 6 + 1 = 7 now.

stepByStep.text: From 2 years ago to 6 years from now is 2 + 6 = 8 years.
His age doubles in those 8 years, so 2 years ago he was 8.
Now he is 8 + 2 = 10.
Check: in 6 years he will be 16, which is twice 8. So Neel is 10 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 8 was Neel's age 2 years ago. Add 2 to come to today.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Two years ago he was 8, and in 6 years he will be 16, which is twice 8. So he is 10 now.
misconceptions.C: 16 will be Neel's age in 6 years. Come back 6 years to today.
misconceptions.D: If Neel were 14, he would be 20 in 6 years, but twice his age 2 years ago would be 24. Try a smaller age.

questionText: Three sisters were born 2 years apart, one after another. Their ages add up to 27 years. How old is the youngest sister?
hints: When ages are equally spaced, the middle one is the equal share. Find the middle age first.
Share 27 equally among the three sisters to find the middle sister's age: 27 ÷ 3.
Example: three brothers born 3 years apart have ages adding up to 45. The middle one is 45 ÷ 3 = 15, so the youngest is 15 − 3 = 12.

stepByStep.text: The middle sister's age is 27 ÷ 3 = 9.
The youngest is 2 years younger: 9 − 2 = 7.
So the youngest sister is 7 years old.

misconceptions.A: 9 is the middle sister's age. The youngest is 2 years younger.
misconceptions.B: 11 is the oldest sister's age. The question asks for the youngest.
misconceptions.C: Right! The sisters are 7, 9 and 11, which add up to 27.
misconceptions.D: 5 takes away 2 twice from the middle age. The youngest is just 2 years younger than the middle sister.

questionText: Five years ago, a family had 4 members and their average age was 19 years. Since then a baby has been born, and no one else has joined or left the family. Today the average age of the 5 members is 20 years. How old is the baby?
hints: Averages hide totals. Find the total of the ages five years ago, then think about how each person has changed since.
Five years ago the 4 members had a total age of 4 × 19 = 76 years. Each of them is 5 years older now. What is their total today?
A similar one: 3 people averaged 20 two years ago, a total of 60. Now they total 60 + 6 = 66. With a new baby the 4 people average 17, a total of 68, so the baby is 68 − 66 = 2 years old.

stepByStep.text: Find the total age of the 4 members five years ago.
Each of the 4 is now 5 years older.
Find the total age of all 5 members today.
The baby's age is the difference.
The baby is 4 years old.

misconceptions.A: 24 is 100 − 76. That compares today's total with the total of five years ago. The four older members have each grown 5 years since then.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The four older members now total 96 years, the family totals 100, so the baby is 4.
misconceptions.C: 1 is the change in the average, from 19 to 20. Work with total ages: 76 then, 96 now for the same four people, and 100 for all five.
misconceptions.D: 19 comes from adding 5 years only once. All 4 members grew 5 years older, which adds 20 years to their total.

questionText: The ages of a father, a mother and their son add up to 75 years. The son is 3 years old. Five years ago, what did the ages of this family add up to?
hints: Go back 5 years for each person separately. Check that each person had been born by then.
The son is 3 now. Where was he 5 years ago? Find what the father and mother add up to now, without the son.
A similar one: a mother, a father and a 2-year-old girl total 82 now. Four years ago the girl was not born. The parents total 80 now, and 4 years ago they totalled 80 − 8 = 72.

stepByStep.text: The son is 3, so 5 years ago he was not yet born.
Find the parents' total now.
Each parent was 5 years younger then.
Five years ago the family's ages added up to 62 years.

misconceptions.A: 60 takes 5 years off all three people. The son is only 3, so he was not born 5 years ago. Take 5 years off the two parents only.
misconceptions.B: Yes! The parents total 72 now, and 5 years ago they were 10 years less in total, which is 62.
misconceptions.C: 70 takes away 5 just once. Each parent was 5 years younger, and the son's 3 years must come out too.
misconceptions.D: 65 takes 5 years off the two parents but still counts the son's 3 years. He was not born yet, so leave him out.

questionText: When Meera was born, her mother was 26 years old. Today her mother is exactly 3 times as old as Meera. How old is her mother today?
hints: The gap between two people's ages never changes. Use the gap together with the 'times as old' clue.
The mother is always 26 years older than Meera. If Meera's age is 1 part and her mother's is 3 parts, how many parts is the gap?
A similar one: a father was 30 when his son was born and is now 4 times as old. The gap of 30 is 3 parts, so one part is 10. The son is 10 and the father is 40.

stepByStep.text: The mother is always 26 years older than Meera.
Meera's age is 1 part and her mother's is 3 parts, so the gap is 2 parts.
Find one part, which is Meera's age.
The mother is 3 parts.
Her mother is 39 years old today.

misconceptions.A: 78 is 26 × 3. But 26 was the mother's age long ago, not Meera's age. Use 26 as the gap between their ages.
misconceptions.B: 13 is Meera's age today. The question asks for her mother, who is 3 times as old.
misconceptions.C: 52 is 26 × 2. Check it: Meera would be 52 − 26 = 26, and 52 is not 3 times 26. The gap of 26 is 2 parts.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Meera is 13 and her mother is 39, which is 3 times 13 and 26 more than 13.

questionText: Anu and Bela are 20 years old together. Bela and Charu are 26 years old together. Anu and Charu are 24 years old together. How old is Charu?
hints: Each child appears in two of the three totals. Think about what you get if you add all three totals.
Add 20, 26 and 24. Every child has been counted twice in this sum, so what do the three ages add up to?
A similar one: P and Q total 10, Q and R total 14, P and R total 12. The sum 36 counts everyone twice, so the three total 18. Then R is 18 − 10 = 8.

stepByStep.text: Add the three totals. Each child is counted twice.
Halve to get the total of the three ages.
Anu and Bela make 20 of this, so the rest is Charu.
Charu is 15 years old.

misconceptions.A: 11 is Bela's age. Take away Anu and Bela's total of 20 from 35 to leave Charu.
misconceptions.B: 9 is Anu's age. Take away Anu and Bela's total of 20 from 35 to leave Charu.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The three ages total 35, and without Anu and Bela's 20 that leaves 15 for Charu.
misconceptions.D: 35 is the three ages added together. Take away Anu and Bela's total to find Charu's age.

questionText: A father is 40 years old. His three children are 4, 6 and 8 years old. After how many years will the father's age be equal to the sum of the ages of his three children?
hints: Each year the father grows 1 year older, but the three children together grow 3 years older. Watch how fast the gap closes.
The children's ages add up to 18 now, so the gap is 40 − 18 = 22. How much smaller does this gap get every year?
A similar one: a mother is 30 and her two children are 5 and 7, a gap of 18. Each year the mother gains 1 and the children gain 2, so the gap closes by 1 a year and takes 18 years.

stepByStep.text: Add the children's ages now.
Find the gap to the father's age.
Each year the children gain 3 years in total and the father gains 1, so the gap closes by 2 years each year.
Find how long the gap takes to close.
Check: the father will be 51 and the children 15, 17 and 19, which add up to 51.
It will happen after 11 years.

misconceptions.A: Yes! In 11 years the father is 51 and the children are 15, 17 and 19, which also add up to 51.
misconceptions.B: 22 is the gap today. The gap does not close by 1 a year: the children gain 3 years in total while the father gains 1, so it closes by 2 a year.
misconceptions.C: 7 comes from dividing the gap by 3. The father also grows older each year, so the gap closes by only 2 years each year.
misconceptions.D: 18 is the sum of the children's ages now. Find how far that is from 40 and how quickly the gap closes.

questionText: A mother was 28 years old when her twin daughters were born. Today the ages of the mother and the two twins add up to 64 years. How old is each twin?
hints: Since the twins were born, three people have been growing older, not two. Count the mother too.
When the twins were born the three ages added up to 28. Every year after that, how much does the total grow?
A similar one: a father was 30 when his twin sons were born, and today the three ages total 60. The total has grown by 30, at 3 years each year, so 10 years have passed and each twin is 10.

stepByStep.text: At the birth of the twins the three ages added up to 28.
Find how much the total has grown since then.
Each year all three people grow a year older, so the total grows by 3.
Check: the mother is 40 and the twins are 12 and 12.
Each twin is 12 years old.

misconceptions.A: 18 shares the extra 36 years between the two twins only. The mother has also grown older, so 36 is shared among three people.
misconceptions.B: 36 is how much the total of the ages has grown. Three people have each grown by the same number of years, so divide by 3.
misconceptions.C: Yes! 12 years have passed: the mother is 40 and each twin is 12, and 40 + 12 + 12 = 64.
misconceptions.D: 9 comes from dividing 36 by 4. Only three people are growing older: the mother and the two twins.

questionText: A father's age and his son's age are written with the same two digits, but in the opposite order. The father is 27 years older than his son, and the son is a teenager (13 to 19 years old). How old is the father?
hints: Test the possible ages one by one. For each age, swap the digits and check both clues.
The son is between 13 and 19. Start with 13: the father would be 31, and 31 − 13 = 18. That gap is too small, so try the next age.
A similar one: a mother and daughter have ages with swapped digits, 36 years apart, and the daughter is under 20. Try 15 and 51: the gap is 36, so the mother is 51.

stepByStep.text: List the son's possible ages, 13 to 19, with the digits swapped for the father: 31, 41, 51, 61, 71, 81, 91.
Find the gap for each pair: 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72.
Only 14 and 41 have a gap of 27.
The father is 41 years old.

misconceptions.A: 52 and 25 are 27 apart and share digits, but then the son would be 25, which is not a teenager. Test the ages from 13 to 19.
misconceptions.B: 63 and 36 are 27 apart, but a son of 36 is not a teenager. Test the ages from 13 to 19.
misconceptions.C: Yes! The son is 14, the father is 41, and 41 − 14 = 27.
misconceptions.D: 74 and 47 are 27 apart, but a son of 47 is not a teenager. Test the ages from 13 to 19.

questionText: Asha is 8 years old. She tells her older sister Bina, 'When I am as old as you are now, you will be 20 years old.' How old is Bina now?
hints: The gap between the sisters stays the same. From 8 to Bina's age is one gap, and from Bina's age to 20 is the same gap again.
Asha needs some years to reach Bina's age. In those same years Bina grows to 20. So Bina's age is exactly in the middle of two numbers. Which two?
A similar one: Ravi is 6 and says that when he is as old as Sam is now, Sam will be 16. Sam's age is halfway between 6 and 16, which is 11. Check: in 5 years Ravi is 11 and Sam is 16.

stepByStep.text: Asha needs a certain number of years to reach Bina's age. In those same years Bina reaches 20.
So from 8 to Bina's age and from Bina's age to 20 are two equal steps. Find the two steps together.
Each step is half of that.
Bina's age is one step above 8.
Check: in 6 years Asha is 14 and Bina is 20.
Bina is 14 years old now.

misconceptions.A: Yes! Bina is 6 years older. In 6 years Asha will be 14, Bina's age now, and Bina will be 20.
misconceptions.B: 12 is 20 − 8, which is two gaps, not Bina's age. Bina is halfway between 8 and 20.
misconceptions.C: If Bina were 16, Asha would need 8 years to reach 16, and Bina would then be 24, not 20. Try the age halfway between 8 and 20.
misconceptions.D: 28 is 20 + 8. Bina will be 20 in the future, so she must be younger than 20 now.

questionText: Ravi's age this year is a multiple of 3. Last year his age was a multiple of 4. Next year his age will be a multiple of 5. Ravi is less than 60 years old. How old is he this year?
hints: Three clues must all be true together. List the ages that fit one clue, then test them against the others.
Start with next year's age, which ends in 0 or 5. So this year's age ends in 9 or 4. Which of those are multiples of 3?
A similar one: an age is a multiple of 4, and one year later it is a multiple of 5, and it is under 20. Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16. Adding 1 gives 5, 9, 13, 17, and only 5 fits. So the age is 4.

stepByStep.text: Next year's age is a multiple of 5, so it ends in 0 or 5. This year's age ends in 9 or 4.
Ages under 60 that end in 9 or 4 and are multiples of 3 are 9, 24, 39 and 54.
Last year's ages would be 8, 23, 38 and 53. Only 8 is a multiple of 4.
Ravi is 9 years old this year.

misconceptions.A: 21 is a multiple of 3 and last year's 20 is a multiple of 4. But next year's 22 is not a multiple of 5. All three clues must fit.
misconceptions.B: 24 is a multiple of 3 and next year's 25 is a multiple of 5. But last year's 23 is not a multiple of 4. All three clues must fit.
misconceptions.C: 39 is a multiple of 3 and next year's 40 is a multiple of 5. But last year's 38 is not a multiple of 4. All three clues must fit.
misconceptions.D: Yes! 9 is a multiple of 3, last year's 8 is a multiple of 4, and next year's 10 is a multiple of 5.

questionText: Ritu and her two brothers are all more than 4 years old. Five years from now, their three ages will add up to 50 years. What did their three ages add up to 2 years ago?
hints: When time moves, every person's age moves. Count how many people there are and how many years you are moving.
From 5 years in the future back to today, each of the 3 children is 5 years younger. Find what the ages add up to today first.
A similar one: in 4 years, two sisters' ages will total 30. Today they total 30 − 8 = 22. Three years ago they totalled 22 − 6 = 16.

stepByStep.text: Go back from 5 years ahead to today. Each of the 3 children is 5 years younger.
Go back 2 more years. Each of the 3 children is 2 years younger.
Two years ago their ages added up to 29 years.

misconceptions.A: 43 takes away 5 + 2 = 7 just once. There are three children, and each one's age changes by 7 years, so the total changes by 21.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Going back 7 years for each of 3 children takes 21 off the total, and 50 − 21 = 29.
misconceptions.C: 35 is what their ages add up to today. The question asks about 2 years ago, so go back 2 more years for each child.
misconceptions.D: 41 goes back 5 years but then forward 2 years. Two years ago is further back, so subtract again.

questionText: A mother is 5 times as old as her daughter. In 6 years, their ages will add up to 60 years. How old is the daughter now?
hints: The 'times as old' clue is about today, but the total is about the future. Bring the total back to today first.
In 6 years both the mother and the daughter will be 6 years older. Take both of those away from 60 to get today's total.
A similar one: a father is 4 times as old as his son, and in 5 years their ages will total 60. Today they total 60 − 10 = 50, which is 5 parts, so the son is 10 and the father is 40.

stepByStep.text: Bring the total back to today. Two people are each 6 years younger.
Today the daughter is 1 part and the mother is 5 parts.
Find one part.
Check: 8 and 40 now, 14 and 46 in 6 years.
The daughter is 8 years old now.

misconceptions.A: 10 is 60 ÷ 6, but 60 is the total in 6 years' time. The mother is 5 times as old today, so find today's total first.
misconceptions.B: 9 comes from taking 6 off the total only once. Both the mother and the daughter will be 6 years older, so take off 12.
misconceptions.C: 40 is the mother's age now. The question asks for the daughter, who is one of the 6 parts.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Today they total 48: the daughter is 8 and the mother is 40. In 6 years they are 14 and 46, which make 60.

questionText: The ages of two cousins multiply to give 84. The older cousin is 5 years older than the younger one. What do their two ages add up to?
hints: List the pairs of numbers that multiply to give 84. Then look for the pair with the right gap.
Some pairs are 2 and 42, 3 and 28, 4 and 21. Keep going and find the gap between the two numbers in each pair.
A similar one: two ages multiply to 40 and are 3 apart. The pairs are 1 and 40, 2 and 20, 4 and 10, 5 and 8. Only 5 and 8 are 3 apart, and they add up to 13.

stepByStep.text: List the pairs that multiply to 84: 1 and 84, 2 and 42, 3 and 28, 4 and 21, 6 and 14, 7 and 12.
Find the gap in each pair: 83, 40, 25, 17, 8 and 5.
Only 7 and 12 are 5 apart.
Add the two ages.
Their ages add up to 19 years.

misconceptions.A: Yes! The cousins are 7 and 12: these multiply to 84, are 5 apart, and add up to 19.
misconceptions.B: 20 is 6 + 14. These multiply to 84, but they are 8 apart, not 5. Keep testing the pairs.
misconceptions.C: 25 is 4 + 21. These multiply to 84, but they are 17 apart, not 5. Keep testing the pairs.
misconceptions.D: 31 is 3 + 28. These multiply to 84, but they are 25 apart, not 5. Keep testing the pairs.

questionText: Kabir's age in months is the same number as his grandfather's age in years. Their ages add up to 78 years. How old is Kabir?
hints: Change both ages to the same unit. Think about how many months make one year.
If Kabir is 1 year old he is 12 months old, so his grandfather would be 12 years old. The grandfather's age is always how many times Kabir's age?

A similar one: a girl's age in months equals her aunt's age in years, and together they are 39 years. The aunt is 12 times as old, so there are 13 parts. One part is 3, so the girl is 3 and the aunt is 36.

stepByStep.text: A year has 12 months, so Kabir's age in months is 12 times his age in years. His grandfather is 12 times as old as Kabir.
Kabir is 1 part and his grandfather is 12 parts.
Find one part.
Check: Kabir is 6 years, which is 72 months, and his grandfather is 72 years.
Kabir is 6 years old.

misconceptions.A: 12 is the number of months in a year. It tells you the grandfather is 12 times as old as Kabir. Share 78 into 13 parts.
misconceptions.B: Yes! Kabir is 6 years, or 72 months, old. His grandfather is 72, and 6 + 72 = 78.
misconceptions.C: 39 is half of 78, but the two ages are not equal. The grandfather is 12 times as old as Kabir.
misconceptions.D: 72 is the grandfather's age in years. Kabir is 72 months old, so change that into years.

questionText: Tara's age and her uncle's age are in the ratio 2 : 5. Six years ago, their ages were in the ratio 1 : 4. How old is her uncle now?
hints: Ages in the ratio 2 : 5 could be 2 and 5, 4 and 10, 6 and 15, and so on. Test these pairs against the clue about six years ago.
Both people must be older than 6. Try 8 and 20: six years ago they were 2 and 14. Is 14 exactly 4 times 2? If not, try the next pair.

A similar one: ages in the ratio 1 : 3 now, and 1 : 5 four years ago. Try 6 and 18: four years ago they were 2 and 14, which is 1 : 7. Try 8 and 24: four years ago they were 4 and 20, which is 1 : 5. So the ages are 8 and 24.

stepByStep.text: List pairs in the ratio 2 : 5 with both ages above 6: 8 and 20, 10 and 25, 12 and 30, 14 and 35, 16 and 40.
Take 6 years off each: 2 and 14, 4 and 19, 6 and 24, 8 and 29, 10 and 34.
Look for the pair where the second is 4 times the first. Only 6 and 24 fit.
That pair comes from 12 and 30, so her uncle is 30 years old now.

misconceptions.A: If the uncle is 20, Tara is 8. Six years ago they were 2 and 14, and 14 is 7 times 2, not 4 times. Try an older pair.
misconceptions.B: If the uncle is 25, Tara is 10. Six years ago they were 4 and 19, and 19 is not 4 times 4. Try another pair.
misconceptions.C: Yes! Tara is 12 and her uncle is 30. Six years ago they were 6 and 24, which is 1 : 4.
misconceptions.D: If the uncle is 40, Tara is 16. Six years ago they were 10 and 34, and 34 is not 4 times 10. Try a younger pair.

questionText: Sarika is born in the year 2006 and Surya is born in the year 2013. In which year will Sarika be twice the age of Surya?
hints: This is an age puzzle. The gap between two people's ages never changes, so think about when the older one can be exactly double the younger one.
First find how many years older Sarika is than Surya, using the years they were born. Then ask how old Surya must be for Sarika's age to be double his.
Similar example: Asha was born in 2001 and Bina in 2005, so Asha is 4 years older. Asha is double Bina's age when Bina is 4 and Asha is 8. Bina is 4 years old in the year 2005 + 4 = 2009.

stepByStep.text: Sarika was born before Surya. Find how many years older she is.
Sarika is always 7 years older. When she is twice Surya's age, that gap of 7 is the same as Surya's age. So Surya is 7 and Sarika is 14.
Surya is 7 years old 7 years after he was born.
Check: in 2020 Sarika is 14 and Surya is 7, and 14 is twice 7. So the year is 2020.

misconceptions.A: In 2017 Sarika is 11 and Surya is 4. Twice 4 is 8, not 11, so try a later year.
misconceptions.B: In 2019 Sarika is 13 and Surya is 6. Twice 6 is 12, which is close to 13 but not equal. Try one year later.
misconceptions.C: Yes! In 2020 Sarika is 14 and Surya is 7, and 14 is exactly twice 7.
misconceptions.D: In 2021 Sarika is 15 and Surya is 8. Twice 8 is 16, so this is one year too late.

questionText: The sum of the ages of a husband and wife 6 years ago was 48 years, The sum of the ages of the husband, wife and son at present is 63 years. What will be the age of the son, 6 years hence?
hints: This is an age puzzle about sums of ages. When time passes, every person in the group grows older, so a sum of ages grows by those years once for each person.
Start with the husband and wife. Their ages added up to 48 six years ago, and both of them are 6 years older now. Find the sum of their ages today.

Similar example: 4 years ago two sisters' ages added up to 20. Each sister is 4 years older now, so today their sum is 20 + 4 + 4 = 28. With their brother the sum today is 33, so the brother is 33 − 28 = 5. In 2 years he will be 5 + 2 = 7.

stepByStep.text: Six years ago the husband and wife together were 48. Each of them is 6 years older now, so add 6 twice to get their sum today.
Today all three together are 63. Take away the parents' 60 to find the son's age now. The trap is to add 6 only once for the two parents.
The question asks for the son's age 6 years from now, not today. He will be 9 years old.

misconceptions.A: Check the parents' sum today. Both the husband and the wife are 6 years older, so 48 grows by 12. Then find the son's age now and add 6.
misconceptions.B: Find the son's age today first by taking the parents' present sum away from 63. Then add 6 years to it.
misconceptions.C: Go one step at a time: the parents' sum today, then the son's age today, then his age 6 years from now.
misconceptions.D: Yes! The parents are 60 together now, so the son is 3 today and will be 9 in 6 years.

questionText: Nikhil is 39 years old and Diya is 32 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 6 years?
hints: This is an age problem. Everybody grows older by the same number of years, so think about each person's age in the future before you add.
Find how old Nikhil will be after 6 years. Then do the same for Diya.

Here is a similar one. Gita is 12 years old and Farhan is 15 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 5 years? Gita will be 12 + 5 = 17 and Farhan will be 15 + 5 = 20, so the sum will be 17 + 20 = 37.

stepByStep.text: After 6 years Nikhil will be 39 + 6 = 45 years old.
Diya will be 32 + 6 = 38 years old.
Now add the two new ages: 45 + 38 = 83. So the sum of their ages after 6 years will be 83.

misconceptions.A: 89 has the 6 years in it one time too many. Make Nikhil and Diya 6 years older, add their two new ages, and then stop.
misconceptions.B: 77 is 39 + 32 + 6, so only one of them got older. Nikhil and Diya each gain 6 years.
misconceptions.C: 71 is 39 + 32, the sum of their ages now. First make each of them 6 years older.
misconceptions.D: Yes! Nikhil will be 45 and Diya will be 38, and 45 + 38 = 83.

questionText: Vivek is 30 years old and Meera is 24 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 4 years?
hints: Both people grow older together. Find each person's new age first, and only then find the sum.
Find how old Vivek will be after 4 years. Then do the same for Meera.
